summary.text: Joseph Hernandez is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee for Comptroller, running against incumbent Thomas DiNapoli. Born in Cuba and a self-described former refugee, he is a biotechnology entrepreneur and investment-firm executive who has not previously held elected office; he ran as an independent candidate for New York City mayor in 2025 before entering the comptroller race. His campaign centers on auditing state spending, creating a fraud task force, and increasing upstate economic investment.

paragraphs.text: Hernandez was born in Camagüey, Cuba, according to his Ballotpedia survey; his campaign website says he fled communist rule at age seven and arrived in the United States, and describes his father as a political prisoner.

According to the website, he attended Florida public schools and earned a B.S. in neuroscience, an M.S. in molecular genetics and microbiology, and an MBA in finance and entrepreneurship, all from the University of Florida.

He also earned an M.S. in chronic disease epidemiology and biostatistics from Yale University. His campaign website lists a master's in global healthcare leadership from the University of Oxford, which a November 2025 news report described as still in progress.
According to his campaign website, Hernandez's career began at Merck & Co. and continued at Affymetrix and then Digene Corp., a maker of an FDA-approved HPV test that was acquired by Qiagen.

He says he has founded, invested in and led more than a dozen biotechnology, healthcare and technology companies, and he is Founder and Senior Managing Partner of the biotech investment firm Blue Water Venture Partners.
According to his campaign website, he is the father of three children.
Hernandez ran as an independent candidate for Mayor of New York City in the November 2025 general election on the Quality of Life Party line, receiving about 0.1% of the vote (1,379 votes).

He announced his run for State Comptroller in November 2025 and was nominated unanimously by the Republican State Committee at its convention in Garden City in early 2026; he also appears on the Conservative Party line.
